concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, when a character dies, the player loses all progress, including items, experience, and levels, forcing them to restart from the beginning. This high-stakes environment compels players to think carefully about their actions and the risks they take during exploration.

In broguece, permadeath is implemented by ensuring that when a player character dies, all progress is lost, requiring the player to restart from the beginning. This mechanic intensifies the tension of exploration and decision-making, as players must weigh risks carefully to avoid losing everything they've gained.

In 'Crawl', permadeath is implemented by ensuring that when a player's character dies, all progress, including experience, items, and levels, is lost, forcing players to start anew with a fresh character. This mechanic heightens the tension of each encounter, as players must weigh the risks of exploring deeper levels against the potential rewards.

In cataclysm-bn, permadeath is implemented by ensuring that when a player's character dies, all progress, including items, skills, and experience, is lost, forcing players to restart from scratch. This heightens the tension of every encounter and decision, as players must weigh the risks of exploration against the potential loss of their character and progress.

definition: A game mechanic where character death is permanent — the player loses all progress and must start a new game. This creates extreme stakes for every decision and fundamentally shapes the risk/reward calculus of gameplay.
exclusion_criteria: Games with respawn mechanics or extra lives
inclusion_criteria: Character death results in permanent loss of the character
No respawn or continue option after death
Progress (items, levels, map knowledge) is lost on death
Player must start a new game after death
title: Permadeath
